# SPD-047 — Bash hook: a git alias in a config file the hook cannot read (-C or --git-dir repo config, HOME or XDG_CONFIG_HOME, ~/.gitconfig) runs a write verb

## Brief
SPD-044 refuses -c/--config-env and environment config injection, but git also reads aliases from config files the hook does not open: another repository's .git/config reached with 'git -C <repo>' or '--git-dir <dir>', the user's ~/.gitconfig, and the global config git finds through HOME ($HOME/.gitconfig) or XDG_CONFIG_HOME ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config) when either is set on the line (Spud added these two at creation; SPD-044 does not read them). A member who can write such a file could define 'alias.p = push' there and then run 'git -C <repo> p' or 'HOME=<dir> git p'. None are configured today (git config --get-regexp alias. is empty), so this is latent, but the hook has no way to read an on-disk alias table.

Evidence: git honours [alias] in any config file it loads; probed at SPD-044 that a GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL file with [alias] v=version makes 'git v' run version. The -C, --git-dir, HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME cases were not probed. Writing another repo's .git/config or ~/.gitconfig is normally outside a member's deliverables (the edit hook refuses it), which limits reach, but a shell redirection into a directory outside the repository may not be. Out of SPD-044's brief, which named it a proposal candidate.

## Size, persona and model decision
One engineer on opus, no children: one hook fix in bin/spud_ledger.py (the git branch of analyse_segment, beside SPD-044's git_line_defines_alias/git_env_defines_alias and SPD-046's program checks) with red-first tests in tests/test_hooks.py, the same shape as SPD-044 and SPD-046, built in worktree spd-047-git-alias-files. Design settled by Spud at start from probes (git 2.54, Apple Git-157): an alias from HOME/.gitconfig, XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config, -C <repo>, --git-dir and GIT_DIR all expand, but git ignores an alias that shadows one of its own commands, so a member's verb outside git --list-cmds=main (an alias, or an external git-<verb> on PATH) is refused; HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME in force are refused like GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, since the file they point at can also name a program (SPD-046's class); -C, --git-dir, --work-tree and GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_COMMON_DIR must resolve inside a checkout the ledger knows.

## Outcome
A member's git call is now refused under Law 7 when its verb is not one of git's own commands (git --list-cmds=main, read with the hook's own environment, cached in the state directory under the git binary's fingerprint, and refused outright when the list cannot be read): git ignores an alias that hides a builtin, so an unknown verb is the tell for every alias source the hook cannot read (another repository's .git/config through -C, --git-dir or GIT_DIR, ~/.gitconfig, XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config, the system config, includes) and for an external git-<verb> on PATH. HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME in force on the line are refused like GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, since the file they point at can also name a program git runs. -C, --git-dir, --work-tree, GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE and GIT_COMMON_DIR must resolve inside a checkout the ledger knows, else refused; unresolvable targets fail closed. Nine older controls that flipped from silent to refused (glob verbs such as git st?tus, git -C /tmp status) were updated with the reason written down. Spud is unaffected. GitAliasFileTest, 13 methods, red first. Differential over 4794 strings: 118 changed, none from refused to silent, none for Spud. Suite 702 OK, rerun by Spud. Merged into main as 64727e4; worktree deleted. Found along the way: SPD-062 (P1, a PATH assignment in force replaces the program the hook checked), SPD-063 (P2, program-naming keys in config files git reads with nothing on the line), and SPD-064 (P1, filed by Spud from Cherie's evidence: a member may write any path outside every registered project).
